approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a persistent tree of molecular graph edits. It purchases the newly expanded frontier directly, records each accepted reward on its actual route, and uses similarity-weighted sibling best returns plus shared completed and pending densities to choose existing branches. After an accepted incumbent improves, it starts a fresh single-root episode at that molecule while retaining the session archive, novelty exclusions and reward scale. Its graph operators, bounded fallbacks and receipt-backed maximum memory already work; there is no active global surrogate or scored-population breeder.
approach.novelty: Remove only the transfer of sibling peak values into exploitation below the virtual root: each branch instead uses its own best accepted return, or the existing neutral default when unobserved. Shared completed and pending densities still determine exploration and unvisited priority. This isolates the value consumer left unresolved when a sibling removed value and density sharing together. Other siblings changed fresh-root membership or excluded certified exhausted support. Keeping density sharing here lets the signed result answer whether deeper value sharing contributes on this exact Parent.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent conflates sibling peak-value transfer with shared completed/pending density in deeper allocation, so the source of its useful sharing remains unidentified. Actual n-e4b751133c75 summary.json and run.log files for all frozen Search seeds are successful: mean 0.49949631467224465, population deviation 0.014066662744436314, and +0.15139519654635733 versus its code Parent. The complete joint deeper-sharing removal n-3f6f7c11f468 falls to 0.447189745055572, a paired loss of 0.05230656961667265, with all seed macros lower. Its confirmed removal supports the combined consumer, not value alone. Older n-4e4e248bd6bd and n-5cc901d1a9e3 change different compositions or both levels and do not resolve this question. An independent own-M/shared-density replay of the actual Parent reproduces 3,460/7,043 changed deeper choices in all fifteen cells, 48,326/52,928 changed exploitation rows, 3,321 unobserved rows with shared completed support, and 2,122/4,350 accepted receipts through changed choices (1,399 late). It finds zero inherited formula or paid-trajectory join mismatches. Sources: policy/scratch/r0056-01-improve-L01-plan/audit-summary.json and its fifteen audit-seed files, each naming the underlying Parent log and trajectory; inputs-sha256.json records the exact files and matches all 16 overlapping frozen Search Policy source hashes. These are actual-state exposure measurements without unpurchased rewards or an alternative adaptive history. The separate formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de remains at 0.607030316211131.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse search-policy-r56-support-and-statistical-consumers and its recorded queries rather than claim a new search. The relevant reviewed RAVE source distinguishes shared value and exploration counts, but its action correspondence and blending assumptions are absent here. The exact removal is justified by internal code, complete Search results and actual-state exposure. RAVE blending, multivalidity and a coherent mean-basis GP remain deferred; the other reviewed sources are not adopted or needed for this tree consumer. No model, dependency or preparation input is introduced.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The intervention follows the actual code Parent n-e4b751133c75, the exposed complete joint removal n-3f6f7c11f468 and the independently reproduced own-M/shared-density action replay. The joint loss does not separate value from density; preserving density while replacing only deeper exploitation answers that measured gap. The original sibling-sharing n-4e4e248bd6bd and peak n-5cc901d1a9e3 panels have different compositions and cannot supply this conditional decomposition. No external algorithmic element is adopted.

sources.applicability: This motivates separating value and density scientifically. Our molecular peak-based sibling kernel is not AMAF: molecular edits need not commute and no Go action-equivalence assumption is adopted. Defer the RAVE blending schedule and any bias constant. Positions 1/2 are internal isolated consumer interventions on existing code, not new RAVE implementations.
sources.finding: Sections 4.1-4.4 distinguish rapidly shared but biased action estimates from direct Monte Carlo returns. UCT-RAVE shares exploitation estimates while equation 18 uses actual action count in exploration; the paper notes the difficulty of justifying shared counts in that exploration term.
sources.title: Monte-Carlo tree search and rapid action value estimation in computer Go (Gelly and Silver, 2011)

hypothesis: At existing-child decisions with parent_id != 0, replace only the exploitation consumer Qbest=B/D with the child occurrence maximum M when its own N>0, otherwise the unchanged neutral default 0.5 (selection_value remains null when unobserved). Keep D=sum_j K_ij*N_j and P=sum_j K_ij*O_j over exactly the original eligible siblings; retain the identical exploration bonus 0.5*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(D+P)), the D+P==0 priority predicate, and earliest-occurrence tie rule. Preserve original B/D and its complete same-state index as a passive reference. For parent_id==0 keep the original shared-peak row and choice law. This is removal of only the deeper off-diagonal peak-value consumer, conditional on active density sharing, within the existing tree identity.

finding_summary.headline: Deeper shared value contributed: its isolated removal reached paid search and reduced mean score by 0.01231.
finding_summary.insights:
This exposed control supports positive conditional contribution from deeper shared peak values when completed and pending density remain shared. It resolves the value-consumer question on this Parent and finite Search panel; it does not separately price density, root sharing, maximum memory or their interactions, and it does not decompose the earlier joint-removal effect. The literature review supplied no adopted external algorithm: this is evidence about the internally defined consumer, not RAVE or a calibrated statistical model. The signed prediction and activation both held, even though the Child did not improve scores.

The method still converts many purchases into small local gains. The Child produced more improvements and 144 fresh-root restarts versus 114, yet less total gain. Fragment-excluded within-cell similarity increased from 0.1923 to 0.2212 overall and from 0.2421 to 0.2877 late; generic scaffold coverage across the panel fell from 1,240 to 1,179, while typed coverage rose from 1,704 to 1,720. These measurements support a shift toward more similar neighborhoods with less productive refinement, rather than wholesale scaffold collapse. The molecular assessment also shows persistent tiny fragments, oversized assemblies and chemically difficult heteroatom connections, despite smaller size tails. Its largest DRD2 loss is associated with a strained nitrogen-ring leader replacing a stronger saturated amino-ring family, but the chemistry does not prove the cause of the score loss. A proposal scheme that preserves useful functional-group relationships while changing topology, or an allocation rule that evaluates useful progress beyond a route maximum, is the kind of method change that could address this limitation. There is no active surrogate whose calibration can be diagnosed here. Whether either method change improves conversion, and whether value sharing transfers to other compositions, remain open. Parent-matched selector timing, formal-run RNG-state invariance and trusted task-safety effects were not measured.
finding_summary.results: The removal operated with shared exploration density and virtual-root choices preserved on every audited state. Own-maximum and shared-value choices differed at 3,427 of 5,689 deeper decisions; changed paths reached 2,029 of 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases, with exposure in all 15 task/seed cells. All 33,785 deeper rows and 10,030 root rows passed the formula and receipt audit. Mean final score fell from 0.49950 to 0.48718, a paired loss of 0.01231, beyond the registered 0.002 scale. Seed differences were −0.03084, −0.01707 and +0.01097. The largest task loss was DRD2 docking, averaging −0.12660; zaleplon, decoration hopping and median-molecule similarity improved on average. The Child made 186 strict improvements versus 148, but their total gain fell from 4.36506 to 4.18039. In the late half, 65 improvements versus 42 produced 1.00761 gain versus 1.36746. All 4,350 emitted terminals joined accepted receipts; none remained censored. The Child also remained 0.11985 below the separate formal Anchor.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich amino-aromatics and heterocycles persist; size extremes shrink, but reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry remain.
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-174737d3e83d against actual code Parent n-e4b751133c75 on frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. context.comparison independently marks Child evaluation complete and Parent pairing complete. All 15 request-listed Child trajectories and 15 published Parent trajectories were read; none was missing. Each task has 900 accepted records, including 870 optimizer outputs; initial molecules are supplied observations, not generated output. Child evidence was read from the exact request-listed .worktrees/slot-1/runs/staging paths. Byte-identical run-local snapshots, original paths and SHA256 hashes are recorded in policy/scratch/r0056-01-improve-L01-molecular/chemistry-reading.json; its sources name each snapshot and published Parent input. The corresponding audit-seed-N-task.json files contain full per-record descriptors, full/late cell counts and source hashes. No future Child archive is claimed. No formal Anchor chemistry comparison was performed. The digest ring-closure presence rates range from 0.8678 to 0.946 and aromatic-token presence from 0.654 to 0.877; these are molecule-level text indicators, not aromatic-atom fractions. The actual graphs include fused and bridged heterocycles, linked aromatics, saturated nitrogen rings, ethers, amides, thioamides, acetals, amines and extensive halogen substitution. Both panels contain 4350 accepted optimizer records. Child/Parent below-six-heavy-atom counts are 312/425 and above-fifty counts 180/301; for late optimizer ordinals 146 through 290 in each cell, the corresponding counts are 125/195 and 83/204 among 2175 records per panel. These reduced tails are descriptive, not a proposed molecular-size gate. Child/Parent distinct nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds are 1720/1704, and generic scaffolds 1179/1240; late counts are 983/974 and 699/725. The panel is structurally broad, but more typed scaffolds do not establish more useful topologies. Fragment-excluded similarity is reported in every cell audit using the same definition: mean all-pairs radius-2, 2048-bit Morgan Tanimoto within the task/seed/window after excluding molecules below six heavy atoms. Conventional medicinal-chemistry motifs coexist with N/O-halogen bonds, peroxides, N-N linkages and crowded small or bridged rings. Explicit peroxide-pattern counts are 334 in the Child versus 171 in the Parent; structural flags alone do not measure instability. Every optimizer SMILES in both panels lacks explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable despite the graph variety, while ordinary amino-aromatic and amide frameworks justify moderate rather than absent medicinal character. RDKit parsed every accepted graph. These files do not measure rejected proposals, internal failed routes, synthetic routes, ionization states, physical binding or timing. Score-gradient readings below describe associations among observed molecules and scores; they neither identify causal chemical contributions nor judge mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer outputs have median 25 heavy atoms and median three perceived rings, with 42 below six heavy atoms and 16 above fifty. Seed 0 reaches a 25-heavy-atom fused nitrogen heteroaromatic carrying a thiocarbonyl ester, hydroxymethyl group and pyridylmethyl substituent (evaluation 262, score 0.4801331038248821). Seed 1 instead reaches a 24-heavy-atom fused N-chloro heteroaromatic with acetyl and tertiary pyridyl carboxamide groups (evaluation 195, 0.4659102597584434). Seed 2 reaches a 25-heavy-atom pyridyl-substituted imine-containing four-membered ring, thiol and unsaturated carbocyclic amide (evaluation 181, 0.4319502594615478). Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant, but the strained rings and N-Cl bond make these unevenly plausible synthetic targets. The published Parent leaders also had 24 or 25 heavy atoms, with fused aryl carboxamide or thioamide frameworks; this is a change of local framework, not newly acquired access to rings.
liabilities: The N-Cl bond and four-membered imine ring warrant stability and preparation scrutiny; graph acceptance does not resolve either.
The thiol/thiocarbonyl chemistry and unspecified saturated-ring stereochemistry complicate interpretation beyond the reported score.
missing_features: Reliable retention of a compact heteroaromatic/polar framework through late edits is missing from the fragment and carbocycle-only outputs, although it is clearly reachable in the leaders.

Chemically conventional alternatives around the high-scoring N-chloro and strained imine-ring neighbourhoods are not established as adequate replacements by these observations; the scores do not identify an absent target-specific motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Higher observed molecules retain a compact multi-ring surface with ring nitrogen and carbonyl or thiocarbonyl functionality. At the low end, OO at seed 0 evaluation 288, N at seed 1 evaluation 217 and NCl at seed 1 evaluation 204 each score zero. The final seed 2 fluorinated unsaturated carbocyclic alcohol scores only 1.5269008183243645e-13. Thus loss of the organized heterocyclic and polar framework accompanies very poor scores, while adding rings or halogens alone is not sufficient. The differing high-scoring oxygen/sulfur and ring-N arrangements prevent attribution to any single group.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer outputs have median 31 heavy atoms and three rings, with 61 below six heavy atoms and 60 above fifty. The seed 0 leader is a 28-heavy-atom substituted aza-aromatic connected through an amidine-like linker to a very small fused ring system; it carries peroxide, O-F and N-Cl linkages (evaluation 281, 0.6319926634350845). Seed 1 reaches three halogen-rich aza-aromatic rings connected by an amine and aryl bond, with a vinyl substituent and acyl fluoride (32 heavy atoms; evaluation 293, 0.6195899772209568). Seed 2 reaches a 38-heavy-atom polyheteroaromatic amide/thioamide with alkoxy-N and N-Cl bonds (evaluation 297, 0.6007178827815279). These are heavily decorated heteroaromatics, not simple missing-ring molecules. Parent leaders were also decorated multi-ring heteroaromatics; Parent above-fifty-heavy-atom outputs numbered 133 versus Child 60.
liabilities: Peroxide, O-F and N-Cl bonds and an acyl fluoride are conspicuous reactive functionalities; multiple such groups in one graph weaken ordinary synthetic plausibility.
The seed 0 leader includes perceived four-membered fused rings, while late large assemblies add substantial structural complexity without establishing useful synthetic access.
missing_features: The low-scoring fragments lack the distributed ring nitrogen, linked aromatic surfaces and polar decoration seen together in the leaders; those relationships are not consistently preserved during structural changes.

High-scoring chemically conventional versions of the peroxide/O-F/N-Cl-rich scaffold families remain unresolved. The trajectories cannot specify a unique absent decoration or prove the reactive connections are required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: CCO at seed 1 evaluation 290, the halogenated nonaromatic ring FC1C=CC(Cl)=C1 at seed 1 evaluation 289, and CCC(C)C at seed 2 evaluation 288 all score 0.5. The highly decorated aza-aromatic leaders score above these minimal frameworks. The final seed 0 small fused aza-ring fragment scores 0.5013189132155105 after losing most substituent and linker context. This supports a local association with assembled ring-plus-decoration patterns, but the narrow score span does not show that reactive bonds themselves are beneficial. The Child has 474 heteroatom-halogen and 239 peroxide pattern occurrences among optimizer molecules, versus Parent 143 and 75, so conventional stability does not track the observed upper score region.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer outputs have median 30 heavy atoms and three rings, with 77 below six heavy atoms and 52 above fifty. Seed 1 produces a comparatively recognizable amino-aromatic framework: a 30-heavy-atom benzo-fused seven-membered N/O ring with a tertiary aliphatic nitrogen, diarylamine connection, alkyl groups and halogen substituents (evaluation 275, 0.9558587367507194). The Parent seed 1 leader has the related N/O-ring and diarylamine framework with an additional fused carbocycle and scores 0.9687642535682931. The Child seed 0 leader instead has two substituted phenyl rings attached to a four-membered nitrogen ring with exocyclic double bonds (24 heavy atoms; evaluation 298, 0.6028545144194377). Seed 2 has two amino/phenol-substituted aromatics joined by an aminoalkene chain and an imidic-acid group (31 heavy atoms; evaluation 221, 0.8095807267576897). Amine centres are plainly accessible; ring closure by itself is not the missing capability.
liabilities: Multiple alkyl and aryl-halogen substituents create considerable nonpolar bulk; solubility and ionization were not measured.

The seed 0 four-membered N ring with exocyclic double bonds and seed 2 aminoalkene/imidic-acid groups raise strain or tautomer questions; the N/O-ring leader also contains an acetal-like N-C-O connection.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently preserve the aromatic-surface/aliphatic-amine relationship across ring and linker changes, even though it reaches that arrangement in a high-scoring series.

Alternative saturated, less strained nitrogen-ring arrangements are underrepresented among the seed 0 leaders compared with its published Parent; these data do not establish a universal required ring or amine pattern.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The very low seed 0 aryl acid/amide at evaluation 39 scores 0.00012284878850374594, and the seed 1 quinoline-containing ether/ketone at evaluation 37 scores 0.0002220008414784072. The strongest observed amino-aromatic leader combines substantial aromatic surface with a separate aliphatic tertiary nitrogen and an arylamino linkage; the acidic amide and ketone/ether examples lack that arrangement. The Child seed 0 strained nitrogen-ring leader is much lower than its Parent seed 0 saturated amino-ring/polycyclic leader at 0.9190747819767275, while seed 1 retains a close high-scoring family. These are local structure-score associations, not proof of protonation, target contact or physical binding.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer outputs have median 34 heavy atoms and five rings, with 66 below six heavy atoms and 42 above fifty. The seed 0 leader is a 37-heavy-atom quinoline/aryl-ether structure connected to a dense N/O-containing polycycle, with an N-O linkage, multiple amide carbonyls and a tertiary ring amine (six perceived rings; evaluation 228, 0.21464436166422118). Seed 1 produces a related carbonyl-rich bridged polycycle with fused aza-aromatic rings, ester and N-N functionality (35 heavy atoms; evaluation 275, 0.2101914901465183). Seed 2 has an alkyl/methoxy-substituted naphthalene connected to a lactam/sulfonamide polycycle (34 heavy atoms; evaluation 285, 0.180658279282991). The Parent also reaches carbonyl-rich aryl polycycles, but its seed 0 best remained the supplied initial fused nitrogen heterocycle at 0.1678386594791329. These graphs contain substantial chemistry; dense bridging and unassigned stereochemistry make their synthesis less straightforward than their functional-group vocabulary suggests.
liabilities: Crowded bridged carbonyl-rich systems, N-O and N-N connections and large fused assemblies lack demonstrated synthetic routes.
Saturated bridgehead and ring stereochemistry are unspecified despite the substantial three-dimensional topology.
missing_features: Small and simplified outputs lose the multi-ring aromatic/carbonyl organization associated with the upper observed scores; the generator does not reliably preserve those relationships while changing scaffold topology.

The output does not establish simpler, synthetically interpretable alternatives with the same useful ring and polar relationships. No specific absent target-like scaffold can be inferred from these low absolute scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied aryl-ether/quinoline amide scores 0.1569767171139282, while the generated seed 0 molecule retains an aryl-ether/aza-aromatic relationship and adds an organized cyclic carbonyl/nitrogen framework at 0.21464436166422118. C at seed 0 evaluation 270 and ClCl at seed 2 evaluation 286 score zero; the late seed 1 small amide at evaluation 300 scores 0.029578550313870453. The low outputs lack the combined aromatic and cyclic polar architecture. Nevertheless the best observed scores remain modest, and the Parent seed 2 differently connected carbonyl-rich framework reaches 0.19720265943665388 versus Child 0.180658279282991. More rings or carbonyls are therefore not an established sufficient explanation.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer outputs have median 22 heavy atoms and two rings, with 66 below six heavy atoms and 10 above fifty. The seed 0 leader is a 24-heavy-atom fluorophenyl-substituted five-membered N-N ring with a cyclobutenol appendage and an N-hydroxy-linked chain of thiocarbonyl groups (evaluation 209, 0.4348013614705566). Seed 2 reaches a chemically distinct 25-heavy-atom amino-acetal cage with N-O chemistry, halogens and a conjugated aminoalkene appendage (evaluation 257, 0.4347074749356297); it has no aromatic atoms. Seed 1 instead reaches a 19-heavy-atom aminofluoroalkyl-substituted pyrrole with unsaturated ether/amine substituents (evaluation 231, 0.23417763960619786). The Parent also reaches small amino/heterocyclic and amino-acetal leaders, with seed 0/1/2 scores 0.4230032077811577, 0.35855114551835887 and 0.36108629330282105. The output samples polar small frameworks, but frequently in unusual thiourea/hydrazine or highly bridged forms.
liabilities: N-N and N-O linkages, repeated thiocarbonyl groups, N-halogen variants and crowded amino-acetals raise preparation or stability questions.
The cage and substituted saturated centres carry no explicit stereochemical assignments; the conjugated aminoalkene variants also leave tautomeric and geometric questions unresolved.
missing_features: Oversized assemblies and late altered cages do not reliably retain the compact size and polar arrangement seen together in the high-scoring small frameworks.

The high-scoring region does not establish ordinary, stereochemically specified alternatives to the N-N/thiocarbonyl and amino-acetal-cage chemistry; the two divergent leaders do not identify a single absent pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The oversized seed 0 multi-aryl ester/thioester assembly at evaluation 171 scores zero, and a related enlarged heterocyclic assembly at evaluation 46 scores 4.7217791475993015e-98. The leaders are markedly smaller while retaining multiple nitrogen/oxygen or thiocarbonyl groups and fluorinated substituents. The aromatic thiocarbonyl leader and nonaromatic amino-acetal leader have nearly equal observed scores, so a universal aromatic-ring requirement is contradicted by this sample. The seed 2 late N-fluorinated cage/unsaturated-ring product at evaluation 300 scores 0.029700209198674284 despite retaining complexity and halogens. The observed gradient is compatible with a balance of size and polar-group arrangement, not a rule to add fluorine, rings or amines indiscriminately.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-174737d3e83d, complete frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, compared descriptively with published code Parent n-e4b751133c75 under the same profile. Among 4350 accepted optimizer outputs, 312 Child molecules have fewer than six heavy atoms and 180 exceed fifty, versus Parent 425 and 301; late counts are 125 and 83 versus 195 and 204 among 2175 per panel. Zero-scoring tiny fragments coexist with very low-scoring large joined assemblies, whereas leaders retain organized rings and polar groups. This updates the Parent-associated output gap with smaller but still present tails; it does not establish a chemical cause of the algorithm contrast.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size changes still fail to preserve useful molecular frameworks consistently, despite reduced fragment and oversized tails.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs access to contraction, expansion and rearrangement moves that retain informative ring and donor/acceptor relationships when possible. Current-session feedback must determine which sizes and arrangements help; these descriptive cutoffs are not universal admission thresholds or an instruction to import a target scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-174737d3e83d on the same complete Search panel, with n-e4b751133c75 as the actual published Parent. Observed leaders include peroxide, O-F, N-Cl, N-O and N-N connections, acyl fluoride, small unsaturated nitrogen rings and crowded amino-acetals. The accepted Child/Parent populations contain 334/171 peroxide-pattern molecules and 704/786 heteroatom-halogen-pattern molecules; these are structural counts, not toxicity or stability scores. Conventional amide, ether and amino-aromatic graphs are also reachable. The persistent output gap is reliable chemically interpretable variation, not an inability to form ordinary functional groups or evidence that reactive motifs caused a score gain.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically conventional alternatives are not reliably available around high-scoring graphs containing reactive heteroatom connections.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conservative bond, heteroatom and linker alternatives around promising topologies so less reactive connections can compete on current-session observations. Do not convert chemical concern into a hidden objective, assume removing a motif improves the score, or claim an unmeasured synthetic route.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-174737d3e83d, frozen Search panel and matched published Parent n-e4b751133c75. High-scoring examples contain separate aliphatic amine and aromatic regions, compact nitrogen heterocycles with carbonyl/thiocarbonyl groups, or organized cyclic polar frameworks. Low-scoring molecules in those observed populations include an acidic aryl amide, an aryl ether/ketone, simple carbocycles and isolated fragments that lack the same relationships. Other high-scoring outputs have no aromatic atoms, so this is a conditional local-neighbourhood observation rather than a universal aromatic pharmacophore. The source is the observed chemistry of this Child/Parent panel, not attribution to their differing statistical consumer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reachable combinations of aromatic surfaces and polar or potentially ionizable centres are inconsistently retained across scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support task-agnostic topology, saturation and linker changes that can preserve functional-group relationships while exploring alternatives. Let accepted feedback within the current session establish where retaining those arrangements is useful; no named benchmark answer, cross-session labels or compulsory motif follows from this association.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-174737d3e83d on frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 and matched Parent n-e4b751133c75. Every task has zero stereocentre-token presence in the Child digest; all 4350 accepted optimizer SMILES in each panel lack explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry. The actual molecules nevertheless contain substituted saturated rings, bridgeheads and amino-acetal cages. This preserves the Parent-associated representation gap; neither the digest nor these trajectories establishes a score penalty from the omission.
transferable_gaps.gap: Generated saturated and bridged frameworks do not distinguish their stereochemical alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Within the existing molecular identity and evaluation contract, a task-agnostic representation would need to preserve and distinguish chemically meaningful stereochemical alternatives rather than leaving every new centre unspecified. Whether that additional chemical distinction changes observed reward remains unmeasured; no stereochemical advantage or target preference is assumed.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
